easy_question: This image was supposed to depict a ruler-and-compass CONSTRUCTION dividing a strip A B into five equal parts: a solid horizontal strip with interior division marks, plus an auxiliary construction ray with equal compass steps above it. Ignoring artistic quality, does the image actually DEPICT that requested subject / carrier / scene -- the physical object, document, board, or diagram it describes? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram of the requested subject ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of the requested subject depicted, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_divisions: The horizontal strip near the bottom of this drafting image (ends labelled A left, B right) is crossed by interior vertical division lines. IGNORE the construction ray, cross marks and arcs above the strip, and do NOT count the strip's own left and right outer edges. The lines may NOT be evenly spaced -- report what you SEE, not what the title asks for. For EACH interior line, estimate its position as a decimal fraction of the distance from A (0.0) to B (1.0), measuring carefully. Answer ONLY the comma-separated list of fractions in increasing order. No other text.
